note: Net names are this fragment's proposal; P2 must reconcile to the final netlist before P5. Design point assumed for all budgets: fsw = 500 kHz, L = 6.8 uH, Vout = 5.0 V, Iout = 3.0 A.

rails.vin: 7-18 V DC at J1 (12 V nominal)

consumers.what: P-channel reverse-polarity FET, drain to input

rails.dissipation_note: worst case at Vin=7 V: Q1 0.208 W + F1 0.238 W; 0.132 W at 12 V

consumers.basis: Iout*sqrt(D(1-D)) rms, peaks at D=0.5 i.e. Vin=10 V (inside range)

consumers.what: EN/UVLO divider, 6.5 V rising / 6.0 V falling

rails.dissipation_note: no dissipating element on this rail itself

consumers.basis: Iout + dI/2 at Vin=18 V, dI = 1.062 A pk-pk

rails.dissipation_note: L1 worst case at Vin=18 V: DCR 0.291 W + core 0.230 W

consumers.basis: STATED spec maximum, delegate Q5 confirms it is the true max

rails.dissipation_note: 3.3 A = 3.0 A spec + 10% design ceiling; rail itself dissipates only the LED
plane return; In1 + In2 + B.Cu all GND

loss_budget_w.spec_point: Vin=12 V, Iout=3 A, Pout=15 W, >88% terminal-to-terminal => Ploss <= 2.045 W
loss_budget_w.worst_total_dissipation: Vin=7 V (1.969 W) - every input-side I^2R term scales with Iin^2 (2.42 A vs 0.93 A) and the HS switch conducts for D=0.714
loss_budget_w.worst_part_dissipation: Vin=18 V - U1 1.001 W (switching ~Vin, LS conduction ~(1-D)) and L1 0.521 W (core ~dI^2)
loss_budget_w.worst_junction_temperature: Vin=7 V (Tj 99.7 C) - board-to-ambient 19 C/W is shared by the TOTAL loss and dominates the IC's own 7 C/W local path

part_parameter_limits.comment: P3 selection limits. Every value is a MAXIMUM (or minimum where marked) that keeps the s2 budget under 2.045 W and Tj under 105 C.

u1_buck_ic.fsw_note: 700 kHz admissible only if (tr+tf) <= 14 ns and Qg <= 4.3 nC
u1_buck_ic.package: MUST be exposed-pad (QFN / HSOIC / HTSSOP). SOT-23-6, SOIC-8 and TSOT-23-8 without a pad are EXCLUDED - they run 100-200 C/W and cannot dissipate 1 W.

l1_inductor.l_note: sized for dI = 0.86 A pk-pk (29%) at 12 V, 1.06 A (35%) at 18 V; requirement is dI <= 1.2 A across the range
l1_inductor.isat_note: must beat the IC's MAXIMUM current limit, not the 4 A minimum spec
l1_inductor.size_note: prefer >= 7.3x7.3 mm molded/composite (theta ~30 C/W); 10x10 mm gives 4 C of relief

q1_pfet.vgs_clamp: MANDATORY 15 V Zener gate-to-source + 100 kOhm gate-to-GND; |Vgs| = Vin up to 18 V steady and ~25 V on a hot-plug ring
q1_pfet.orientation: drain to input, source to load (only orientation that blocks a reversed supply)
q1_pfet.gate_rc: NONE - the body diode is forward-biased in the normal direction, so a gate RC cannot limit inrush

f1_fuse.i2t_note: hot-plug demands 0.058-0.19 A^2s; >= 8x margin at 1.5-4 A^2s typical

cin.bulk_esr_note: ESR is a DAMPING requirement, not a loss: a <20 mOhm polymer removes the cable-LC damping and pushes hot-plug ringing to ~25 V. Use a 105 C aluminum electrolytic.

cout.note: ripple <50 mV pk-pk and the 200 mV load step drive the value, not the loss

all_mlcc.reason: board surface sits at 83-87 C; X5R (85 C) is NOT acceptable anywhere on this board

power_constraints._comment: raw input, J1 -> F1 -> Q1 drain, BEFORE the reverse-polarity element: width-only entry, nothing decouples it by design. IPC-2152 needs 1.52 mm on 1 oz outer at dT=10; route 1.8 mm. dT=10 not 20 because the local board temperature is already 83-87 C.
protected input rail, Q1 source -> Cin bank -> U1 VIN pin. Decoupled (hot loop) so it stays in the check_pdn inventory. Same 1.8 mm width.

3.0 A + dI/2 at Vin=18 V. IPC-2152 needs 2.31 mm on 1 oz outer. Resolve against the EMI containment rule by making SW a SHORT WIDE POUR: >=2.5 mm wide, <=8 mm long, <=40 mm^2, F.Cu only, never inner, never near a board edge or connector.
3.0 A spec + 10% ceiling. IPC-2152 needs 2.06 mm on 1 oz outer; route 2.5 mm. Any layer transition would need 7 vias - design for none, keep it all on F.Cu.

DECLARED EXPLICITLY on purpose: at 3.3 A check_current would otherwise only synthesize an advisory return-net entry. Declared, pour necks stay ERROR at the full budget. No neck below 2.1 mm in the output-return path. In1 + In2 + B.Cu are all GND.

thermal_constraints._comment: 1.001 W is the Vin=18 V worst case. dt_c 55 = Tj_design 105 C (125 C spec floor - 20 C margin) above 50 C ambient. check_thermal's model needs >= 529 mm^2 of GND copper within 14.3 mm of U1 summed over layers to pass; target >= 650 mm^2 (its A_sat). NOTE: the via warning will NOT fire at dt_c/power_w = 55 > 51.1, so the 16-via array is a P6/P7 requirement enforced by review, not by the script.

0.521 W is the Vin=18 V worst case (DCR 0.291 + core 0.230). Heatsink net is the output-side pad pour. Needs >= 194 mm^2 by the model. Hand analysis: surface ~103 C, so the part must be rated >= 125 C.

thermal_case.airflow: none, natural convection, open frame, both faces exposed
thermal_case.r_ba_derivation: A_eff = 2 faces * 2000 mm^2 * 0.85 shadowing = 3400 mm^2; h_conv = 1.42*(37/0.05)^0.25 = 7.4 W/m2K; h_rad = 0.9*sigma*(Ts^2+Ta^2)(Ts+Ta) = 8.2 W/m2K; R = 1/(15.6 * 3.4e-3). Radiation is 53% of the cooling.
thermal_case.spreading_note: k*t = 0.0336 W/K with In1+In2+B.Cu near-solid; lambda = sqrt(k*t/2h) = 33 mm > board half-dimension, so the board is near-isothermal and the WHOLE outline is the heatsink.
thermal_case.tj_limit_rationale: 125 C junction spec (the floor across candidate families; most spec 150 C) minus 20 C design margin. Margin is 20 not 25 because 50 C ambient is a hard spec maximum and the 99.7 C figure is already worst-of-worst-cases.

sensitivity.plain: every extra 100 mW anywhere on the board costs 1.9 C of junction temperature - the loss budget IS the thermal budget

thermal_case.exposed_pad_alone: 6 mm^2 of F.Cu -> theta_JA 138 C/W -> Tj 188 C. The pad does NOT close it; the planes do. (Confirms the brief's warning quantitatively.)
thermal_case.two_oz_copper_verdict: 2 oz outer does NOT help thermally - R_ba is set by area and h, and the board is already isothermal at 1 oz (<5% gain). Spend the Q21 escalation only if IPC-2152 widths cannot be routed.

copper_sizing_ipc2152.dt_rationale: IPC-2152's rise is above the LOCAL board temperature, which s4 puts at 83-87 C. A 20 C rise would put trace copper at 105 C. The 10 C widths route fine here.
copper_sizing_ipc2152.inner_layer_verdict: 0.5 oz inners need 3.0-4.6 mm per net - unusable as power planes. In1 AND In2 must both be solid GND; no power net on an inner layer. All power stays on F.Cu (single-sided assembly makes this natural).

inrush.case: hot-plug of an 18 V supply into a discharged 120 uF input bulk through a 1 m cable
inrush.verdict: BENIGN for Q1. Do NOT fit a gate RC.
inrush.why: Q1 is drain-to-input / source-to-load (the only reverse-blocking orientation), so its BODY DIODE is forward-biased in the normal direction. The bulk charges through the diode and the channel plays no part - a gate RC cannot limit inrush, it only delays a channel the diode has already bypassed.

q1_stress.soa_verdict: 1-2 orders inside the single-pulse SOA of any SO-8/DFN P-FET

required_instead: MANDATORY Vgs clamp: 100 kOhm gate-to-GND + 15 V Zener gate-to-source. |Vgs| = Vin, 18 V steady and ~25 V on a ring; a 20 V-Vgs part has no margin on the ring. Bias loss 0.54 mW at 18 V.

Ringing overshoot at U1 VIN: zeta = (R/2)*sqrt(C/L). R=0.30 Ohm -> 18.0 V (overdamped); 0.10 -> 20.3 V; 0.05 (short cable, all-ceramic Cin) -> 25.4 V. This is why delegate Q6 requires IC abs-max >= 28 V and input MLCCs >= 50 V.
Bulk-cap ESR is a DAMPING requirement: 50-300 mOhm. A low-ESR polymer bulk would remove the damping and push the ring toward 25 V.
Fuse survives: I^2t = I_pk^2*tau/2 = 0.058 A^2s (0.30 Ohm) to 0.19 A^2s (0.10 Ohm) vs 1.5-4 A^2s melting I^2t for a 4 A time-lag part - >= 8x margin, no nuisance opening.
OMIT the gate capacitor: it buys nothing on inrush and would delay turn-off on a polarity reversal while running.

thermal_via_array.plus: ring of 8-12 stitching vias at 1.2 mm pitch in the surrounding F.Cu GND island (outside the pad, no paste concern)
thermal_via_array.cross_check: Wurth FEA array table (11x11 pad, 1.6 mm, 2-layer, via-to-bottom): 9 -> 7.3 C/W, 16 -> 5.2 C/W, 25 -> 3.8 C/W (ai-library/pcb-verification-standards-2026). That is the full 1.6 mm on 2 layers; this 4-layer stackup reaches In1 at 0.21 mm, so 1.9 K/W is right here and 5.2 C/W is the conservative bound.
thermal_via_array.fab: 0.3 mm is JLC standard-class minimum drill. Tent with soldermask on the BOTTOM side to stop solder wicking; do not buy filled-and-capped via-in-pad. Windowpane U1's paste aperture (4-9 sub-apertures, ~60-70% area) so the array does not float the part.

required_copper_area.F.Cu: GND thermal island contiguous with U1's exposed pad, >= 100 mm^2 (e.g. 10 x 10 mm), not fragmented by SW or VIN routing
required_copper_area.In1.Cu: solid GND, NO split within 12 mm of U1 (>= 400 mm^2 in that radius) - the brief's uninterrupted plane under the switching components, and only 0.21 mm below the pad
required_copper_area.In2.Cu: GND as well, NOT a power plane (>= 400 mm^2 under U1)
required_copper_area.B.Cu: GND pour >= 1500 mm^2 of the 2000 mm^2 outline - the second radiating face
required_copper_area.check_thermal_target: GND copper within a 14.3 mm radius of U1, summed over layers, >= 650 mm^2 (its A_sat); >= 529 mm^2 is the bare pass

other_parts.F1: >= 20 mm^2 per pad, kept off the U1/L1 zone

layout_notes: Hot loop (buck.md s3): Cin ceramic -> U1 VIN -> U1 PGND -> Cin, shortest loop on the board, all on F.Cu, with a 100 nF HF bypass AT the VIN pin. In1 solid GND directly beneath as the image plane.
SW containment (buck.md s5): SW is a short wide pour - >= 2.5 mm wide for IPC-2152, <= 8 mm long and <= 40 mm^2 for EMI. F.Cu only. Away from the board edge and from both connectors (brief).
Input and output on opposite short edges (delegate Q10), straight-through power flow, so the noisy input loop and the output terminal are maximally separated.
Place the bulk aluminum electrolytic at the INPUT edge - the coolest corner (~80 C local vs 87 C mean) - because its life is set by board temperature.
In1 AND In2 both solid GND. No power net on an inner layer (0.5 oz needs 3.0-4.6 mm). This is simultaneously the thermal answer, the EMI answer and the IPC-2152 answer.
Test points: SW tap is a short stub that must NOT extend SW copper (it counts against the 40 mm^2). VOUT test pad paired with a scope-ground pad ~5 mm away (delegate Q13).
DNP RC snubber footprint across the low-side switch (SW to PGND) must be routable with low inductance even unstuffed (brief).
No layer transitions on VIN / +VIN / SW / +5V - a transition would need 6-8 vias at 0.5 A/via. GND is plane-fed through the stitching field.
Thermal-via array under U1 is NOT enforced by check_thermal at these constraint values (dt_c/power_w = 55 > 51.1) - it is a review-enforced P6/P7 requirement.
